Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 101 s. 2021 09 August 2021 HON. HECTOR C. AMARO Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Hinabangan HON. RONEL A. PAZON Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Hinabangan HON. ARTHUR A. ABAN Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Hinabangan HON. RODOLFO N. CALUTAN Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Hinabangan GENTLEMEN: This pertains to your letter dated 06 May 2021 requesting for the Department's appropriate action on the alleged withholding of salaries and allowances of all Sanggunian Bayan members as the Municipality is currently operating on a re- enacted budget. Based on your letter, Mayor Elena M. Dieza issued Memorandum Order No. 4, series of 2021 on 26 February 2021 entitled "ORDER WITHHOLDING THE ACTUAL RELEASE OF THE REMUNERATION OF ALL SANGGUNIANG BAYAN MEMBERS AS PROVIDED UNDER SECTION 323 OF R.A. 7160". It was alleged that the said Memorandum Order is anchored on Sections 319, 323 and 444 of the Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the Local Govemment Code of 1991 (LGC). To provide you definitive guidance on the matter, we deem it proper to revisit Section 323 of the LGC, thus: "Section 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the sanggunian concemed fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

be taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concemed. However, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. In the implementation of such reenacted ordinance, the local treasurer concemed shall exclude from the estimates of income for the preceding fiscal year those realized from nonrecurring sources, like national aids, proceeds from loans, sale of assets, prior year adjustments, and other analogous sources of income. No ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations shall be passed in place of the annual appropriations. In case the revised income estimates be less than the aggregate reenacted appropriations, the local treasurer concemed shall accordingly advise the sanggunian concemed which shall, within ten (IO) days from the receipt of such advice, make the necessary adjustments or reductions. The revised appropriations authorized by the sanggunian concemed shall then be the basis for disbursements. " (Emphasis ours) Section 323 is unequivocal when it provides that the annual appropriations for: (1) salaries and wages of existing positions; (2) statutory and contractual obligations; and (3) essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and funds for these shall be disbursed in accordance with the reenacted budget. Moreover, the representation allowance and travelling allowances (RATA) in its nature, are distinct but complementary allowances provided to select government officials to cover related expenses incidental to and in connection with the actual performance of their respective functions.l This is an entitlement for those holding regular positions.2 Thus, it is part and parcel of the incumbent's salary and wages. Based on the foregoing it is clear that the Memorandum Order No. 4, Series of 2021 issued by Mayor Elena M. Dieza is not in accordance to the aforequoted provisions of the Local Govemment Code of 1991. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter.
